fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Lamentations, Tammuz and the Bacchus Cycle", "body": "Chance said the episode title pointed to the Book of Lamentations and the prophet Jeremiah, and he read the name as Yah, Rah and Maya. He quoted a passage from one of Dylan Saccoccio's Spirit Whirled books about women weeping for Tammuz in July, and compared that mourning to Osiris and Bacchus. Chance argued that Loki played the Bacchus figure and that the weeping season matched the sun's decline from Leo through Virgo toward Libra. He also drew the episode's frame from the Book of Lamentations verses on the cut off horn."}, {"title": "One Name, Many Gods Through Letter Swaps", "body": "Chance said the crowd of gods in mythology came mostly from epithets and letter swaps that scholars mistook for separate beings. Over the episode he proposed that Tyche and Dike were one figure, that Lady Justice and Fortuna were one figure under different names, and that GBL, the number 35, led toward gavel and Bible. Gabe offered Themis as an anagram of Metis and said the epithets all described the same figure. Chance also tied nexus, ligare and lex into one story about law as religion."}, {"title": "The Adjustment Card and the Fornax Sky Map", "body": "Gabe brought Crowley's book on the Adjustment card, including the letter Lamed, the Lambdoma and a link to Notre Dame, and he kept pointing to the Fornax constellation, tying it to the river lyrics of the opening song. He also pointed to the orb in the sky as the card's orb. Chance read Crowley's line that the marriage of opposites was the annihilation of illusion and asked whether joining the masculine and feminine destroyed or created everything. One of the hosts said the meteor bunker had the shape of the Fornax constellation."}, {"title": "Wine, Fans and the Savior in the Basket", "body": "Chance connected the grape harvest in Virgo and pressing in Libra to the Lamentations imagery, to Loki throwing Sylvie into a barrel, and to the purple color grading. Gabe added Diogenes in his wine barrel as the Crater constellation and the Canes Venatici dogs. Chance later read the winnowing fan as a cradle, an ark and an oar, linked it to Venus, and traced the heart symbol to the silphium plant, noting that the name sounded like Sylvie, whom he called the silver moon to Loki's sun."}, {"title": "Stasis Versus Flow as Two Equilibriums", "body": "Chance closed with his main thesis that equilibrium could mean the stasis of death, as he understood Crowley's description, or the flow of exchange, which he compared to the water cycle. He said both readings were true and that nature respected either choice, and he read a viewer's note that the Pythagoreans called 35 harmony. One host called the nostalgia spell an explicit definition of entertainment, and Chance said entertainment literally meant to enter and hold the mind. The hosts closed by reading the TemPad as a pad and tab that kept tabs on a person."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Slick and I pick up the Marvelous DeMystifiers trail once again! The third episode of Loki conceals some dark Disney dealings, a path to deeper understanding of the Justice card of the major arcana, the prophet Jeremiah and the book of Lamentations, and a revelation of the misguided magical reasons for all the gender bending pushed in society.
